clue.text: Immediately make up for involving Conservative

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: to atone is to make amends for a wrong
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: An urgent demand that someone compensate straight away for dragging a Tory into something.
explanation.walkthrough: C sits inside ATONE to give AT ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday adverbial synonym meaning without any delay.

clue.text: Express route in America about New Haven emptied

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for America

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is cleared, so just the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters before it are reworked

parts.note: the five letters reordered

explanation.surface: Directions to a fast road in the US, passing by a deserted New Haven in Connecticut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Haven' is the Connecticut city in the surface, but the two words split: New shuffles the word about, and Haven loses its middle. A then sits between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, a high-speed express road.

clue.text: Fruit-growing location, alternatively nettle yard

parts.note: or offers an alternative
to nettle someone is to anger them
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A gardener choosing between a fruit house and a weedy yard full of nettles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettle' looks like the plant in this horticultural scene; it is the verb meaning irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glasshouse built for growing orange trees, so a place where fruit is grown.

clue.text: Playing nice chess around hot creek, wild board game

indicators.note: playing about with something moves its parts, so the letters are mixed
wild means out of control, so the letters run into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friendly game of chess played somewhere beside a steamy creek in the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters are mixed together; 'around' just strings the surface along.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese chequers is a star-shaped board game played by moving marbles or pegs, an example of a board game.

clue.text: Offer support, repulsing the French therefore

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: repulsing means driving back, so the words that follow are turned round

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)
so means therefore

explanation.surface: Someone backs a plan while rebuffing the French, and so the matter is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repulsing' governs both 'the French' and 'therefore', taken together as one chunk before reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for consideration, a noun synonym of an offer.

clue.text: City tango is great success

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city
T is tango in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Dancing the tango in a Brazilian city is a big hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot can mean an outstandingly entertaining hit, as in 'the show was a riot'.

clue.text: For each offspring, I lie about adult representation

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the next

parts.note: per means for each
a son is offspring
taken as written
a fiction is an untruth
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A parent confesses to fibbing about each child's grown-up status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' is the noun, an untruth, not the verb meaning to recline.
explanation.definitionFit: Personification is the depiction of an abstract idea in human form, a kind of representation.

clue.text: Governing body chosen at election internally

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the letters lie within the words given

parts.note: the letters run across the first three words

explanation.surface: A legislature picked by a vote of its own members.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative assembly, one kind of governing body.

clue.text: Strong urge in pool to pocket black one

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so the next pieces go within the first

parts.note: a lido is a public open-air swimming pool
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A snooker player's urge to sink the black ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' and 'pocket' suggest the cue game, but pool is a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire or drive, a powerful instinctive urge.

clue.text: Very sad time for one, Havana in revolution

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word is written from the end

parts.note: a Havana is a cigar, one example of the kind

explanation.surface: A gloomy moment for someone as Cuba's capital is gripped by revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Havana' looks like the Cuban city, but it is the cigar named after it; 'for one' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes something causing deep sorrow, a stronger synonym of very sad.

clue.text: Badly born, do OK getting means of entry

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone born into poor circumstances does fine and gains a foothold in society.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a social-mobility story; the 'means of entry' is literal hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorknob is the handle you turn to open a door, so it is how you get in.

clue.text: English deserter caught by odd mistake

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so the word before goes into the one after

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: An English army deserter is captured through a strange error.
explanation.walkthrough: Rat for a deserter comes from the belief that rats leave a sinking ship; rum meaning odd is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing or writing, a formal word for a mistake.

clue.text: Insect carries pokers

parts.note: a bug is an insect
bears means carries

explanation.surface: A beetle hauling fireplace irons, an absurd little scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pokers' looks like fire irons; here they are things that poke or goad you, irritations.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugbears are persistent annoyances, things that prod at you like goads, hence pokers.

clue.text: Disputed low tide sprays without current

indicators.note: spray scatters things about, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle
taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A shallow tide throwing up spray when there is no current flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for the tide, but it is the verb for what cattle do.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooted means raised for debate or argued over, so a mooted point is a disputed one.

clue.text: Desiring endless relief from pain

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: aspiring means hoping for or desiring

explanation.surface: Someone longing endlessly for respite from pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkiller, so taking it brings relief from pain.

clue.text: Shore buffeted two ships showing skill in managing bays, perhaps

indicators.note: something buffeted is knocked about, so the letters are battered into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
MAN is a ship in names like merchantman and man-of-war, followed by SHIP itself

explanation.surface: A coastline battered by a pair of vessels, apparently a display of seamanship around coastal inlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bays' looks like coastal inlets in a nautical scene, but bays are brown horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsemanship is the art of handling horses, and a bay is a reddish-brown horse, an example.

clue.text: Unnecessarily loose, it disturbed morality finally

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone with loose morals is needlessly upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no purpose, so otiosely means superfluously or needlessly.

clue.text: Broad church backing Glasgow team, first half over

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation before it is read from the end
turned over means flipped, so only the opening half of the team's name is written backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Celtic is a Glasgow football club

explanation.surface: A broad church supporting a Glasgow football side, with the first half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad church' looks like one phrase but splits: broad is the definition. Celtic's first half CEL is reversed, TIC kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic means drawing on a wide range of sources, so broad in scope or taste.

clue.text: Nationalist talk surrounding upper-class French wine is focus for Nice

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose, so the first word wraps the following ones

parts.note: to chat is to talk
U is the old label for upper-class usage
vin is French for wine
taken as written

indicators.note: the focus is the very centre, so only the middle of the next word is kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A patriotic speech in Nice extols posh French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' wants to be the French city in this French-flavoured surface; it is just a word whose middle is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Chauvinism originally meant fanatical patriotism, so a chauvinistic person is an aggressive nationalist.

clue.text: Played with guy outside mouth of Mississippi Delta

indicators.note: outside means around, so the first word wraps the next

parts.note: a guy is a rope securing a tent or mast

indicators.note: a river's mouth is where it begins its exit, read here as its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the river's name
D is delta in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone frolicked with a man near where the great river meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth of Mississippi Delta' reads as geography, but delta is the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp is to play boisterously, so romped means played about.

clue.text: Presents loaf of wet rusk occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: A baker hands out bread and soggy biscuits now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer is to present or hold something out, so offers is the verb presents.

clue.text: Eliminate waste in Washington bureau

parts.note: to off someone is slang for to kill or eliminate them
in American slang to waste or ice someone is to murder them

explanation.surface: A call to cut wasteful spending in a US government department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Washington' flags the American slang sense of waste, meaning to kill, not the overspending the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a government department or agency, a synonym of office in that sense.

clue.text: Leg advanced towards the front in item of clothing

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
fore means at or towards the front

explanation.surface: A leg pushed forward in a garment, as if stepping out in a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless apron or dress worn over other clothes, an example of a garment.

clue.text: Spots a shape, not ordinary

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for the next word is removed

parts.note: a cone is a solid shape
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: Pimples form an unusual pattern on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is the skin condition marked by pimples, so spots in the medical sense.

clue.text: Before fraught broadcast show

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: fraught means anxious and strained

explanation.surface: A nervy moment before a programme goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a TV studio; 'show' is the definition, not the programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretence is a false display or outward appearance, a noun sense of show as in 'all for show'.

clue.text: Straight order

definitions.meaning: first meaning: without deviation, going the shortest way
second meaning: to instruct or command

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a plain instruction; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for going without a detour and a verb for giving someone instructions.

clue.text: Orchid, spliced with Michaelmas daisy, is failure

indicators.note: splicing joins two ends by overlapping them, so one shared letter is used only once

parts.note: disa is a genus of African orchids
the Michaelmas daisy is a kind of aster

explanation.surface: A gardener's attempt to cross two flowers ends in flop.
explanation.walkthrough: The A that ends DISA is the same A that begins ASTER, so the two words overlap.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a complete fiasco, an emphatic synonym for a failure.

clue.text: Harmonious insolvency arranged, though no love lost

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are reordered
with the word for affection taken away, those letters vanish from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bankruptcy settled amicably even though the parties dislike each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No love lost' is an idiom for mutual dislike; here it literally removes L, O, V, E from INSOLVENCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in sync means moving or acting in step together, an idiom for harmonious.
